Following 88 Legislative Council members' first trip to Beijing last week for a "study and investigation" programme, district service and care team leaders are also receiving "training" in the mainland. As the trend of going north for study and training gathers pace, Collective Discourse reviewed the past year and found that different government departments have undertaken at least nine study or training trips to the mainland, covering the legislature, permanent secretaries, care teams, criminal prosecution personnel, information officers, as well as the civil aviation, education, information technology and cybersecurity sectors.

88 Legislative Council members went to Beijing last week for a "study and investigation programme", and this week it is the turn of district service and care team leaders to take part in a "mainland training course". (Photo courtesy of the Information Services Department)

Under the principle of "patriots governing Hong Kong", going north for study, investigation and training has become the norm. Last week, all 88 Legislative Council members went to Beijing for a "closed-loop" study and investigation programme — the first such trip since the handover. Collective Discourse used keywords such as "study" and "training" to search the government news website and various departments' social media platforms, and found that in the past year, government departments have undertaken at least ten study and training trips to the mainland.

The government issued a statement today (27th) stating that Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak will travel to Beijing this afternoon, and will attend the opening ceremony of the first session of the "mainland training course" for leaders of Hong Kong district service and care teams.

The week-long study programme was conducted entirely under a "closed-loop" arrangement, with members prohibited from leaving on their own, except for investigation visits. (Photo courtesy of the Information Services Department)

88 members attend "closed-loop" study programme; Xia Baolong meets them and urges enhanced learning

Apart from the "district governance" teams requiring training, Legislative Council members are no exception. Excluding Raymond Wong, who resigned due to drunk driving, and Election Committee constituency member Erin Yim, who took leave for "personal reasons", all 88 members departed on 19 July for the study and investigation programme and returned to Hong Kong on 25 July after completing the week-long itinerary. Legislative Council President Starry Lee described it before departure as a "historic" study and investigation trip to Beijing for members, with great significance, saying it was a good opportunity for members to understand the country's latest developments and national conditions and policies, and she believed it would help in preparing Hong Kong's first five-year plan.

The seven-day itinerary was conducted entirely under a "closed-loop" arrangement, with members prohibited from leaving on their own, except for investigation visits. According to a statement issued by the Legislative Council Secretariat, the members' seven-day itinerary included attending lectures at the National Academy of Governance on implementing the overall national security concept, enhancing social governance, analysis of the international relations situation, "Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era", and the "15th Five-Year Plan"; they also received teaching at the Museum of the Communist Party of China, and visited the Beijing Citizen Service Hotline Centre, as well as undertaking projects to investigate new quality productive forces and primary-level legislation.

One day before returning to Hong Kong, State Council Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office Director Xia Baolong met with the members, encouraging them to strengthen their learning and unity, and stating that under the new circumstances, the Legislative Council should "play a better role" in supporting the Chief Executive and the Hong Kong government in governance. After returning to Hong Kong, Starry Lee described the trip as "extremely rewarding", and said "the experience of living together this time is a priceless gain", adding that members would apply what they had learned and put it into practice.

Before the itinerary ended, Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office Director Xia Baolong met with members, stating that under the new circumstances members should "play a better role". (Photo courtesy of the Information Services Department)

Permanent secretaries and department heads undertake "study programme" again after 2023

The Civil Service Bureau has repeatedly stressed that through different types of training and exchange programmes, civil servants can gain a deeper understanding of national conditions. On 19 April this year, Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung led more than 20 permanent secretaries and department heads to Beijing and Chengdu to participate in a study course and investigation trip. This was the second time since 2023 that the Hong Kong government had arranged for permanent secretaries and department heads to undertake study programmes in the mainland, and it was stated that the purpose was to deepen understanding of major national policies and development strategies, and to promote working ties and exchanges between officials from both places.

According to information, the visit included studying "Xi Jinping Thought", the "15th Five-Year Plan", the international situation and China-US relations at the National Academy of Governance after arriving in Beijing; they were also received by State Council Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office Director Xia Baolong. Ingrid Yeung expressed gratitude for Xia Baolong's full affirmation of the civil service's work, and said the team would proactively align with the national 15th Five-Year Plan. The team then travelled to Chengdu for an investigation trip, meeting with leaders of the Sichuan provincial government, and visiting the National Supercomputing Centre in Chengdu, low-altitude economy enterprises, revitalised old factory industrial parks, the Wenjiang Hi-Tech Industrial Park, the Giant Panda Breeding Research Base, and the Sanxingdui Museum, among other sites.

Earlier this month (5th), Ingrid Yeung also set off for Guangzhou to attend the opening ceremony of a civil service training course.

In April this year, after 2023, Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung again led more than 20 permanent secretaries and department heads to participate in a study programme, before travelling to Chengdu for an investigation trip. (Photo courtesy of the Information Services Department)

Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao jointly holds "Criminal Prosecution Study Programme"; two "mainland visits" in the year

In July this year, the three places of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao held the first three-day "Criminal Prosecution Study Programme" in Shenzhen. Secretary for Justice Paul Lam described the programme as "of far-reaching significance", marking professional exchange among the three jurisdictions. He noted that the programme focused specifically on comparing the criminal prosecution systems of the three places, and that prosecution personnel from the three jurisdictions would conduct a mock trial prosecution and defence based on the same case involving a telecommunications network fraud, in order to understand each other's judicial systems and practical operations. Paul Lam said that this study programme "can be regarded as a new starting point for implementing the requirements of the '15th Five-Year Plan' and strengthening legal exchange and cooperation in the Greater Bay Area".

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam delivered a speech at the first Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Criminal Prosecution Study Programme in early July this year. (Photo courtesy of the Department of Justice)

In addition to the study programme, the Department of Justice also made two "mainland visits" during the year. In March this year, Paul Lam led a delegation of about 40 people — comprising representatives from the Law Society, the Bar Association and others — on a two-day visit to Shanghai, where they visited the headquarters of an internet technology company, met with the local vice mayor, officials from the Justice Bureau, and the vice president of the Higher People's Court, among other exchanges; they then travelled to Hangzhou to engage with representatives of the legal profession in Zhejiang Province, and visited the City Exhibition Hall of the Sci-Tech City, among other activities.

In late April, Paul Lam also led the Director of Public Prosecutions, the International Law Commissioner, the Law Policy Commissioner, the Civil Law Commissioner, as well as government counsel from various legal divisions to Beijing, visiting the Supreme People's Court and several central ministries and commissions to discuss and exchange views on the Department of Justice's main policy initiatives; they also discussed with the Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Basic Law Committee of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the implementation of the Constitution and the Basic Law in Hong Kong, and introduced the Department of Justice's work to the Deputy Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office, among other matters.

In May this year, the People's Public Security University of China held the 120th session of the "Hong Kong Police Mainland Study Programme", with 28 participants receiving training. (University website photo)

Immigration Department sent 257 personnel for study and training last year; police mainland study groups totalled 122 sessions

Some disciplined services also regularly send personnel to the mainland for national conditions training. According to the People's Public Security University of China website, in accordance with the Ministry of Public Security's 2026 "Hong Kong and Macao Disciplined Services Training Plan", the university held the 120th session of the "Hong Kong Police Mainland Study Programme", with 28 participants receiving training. According to the Hong Kong Police publication "Police Bulletin", in June this year, 28 police officers went to the Shanghai Public Security College to attend the 122nd mainland study group, a 12-day course covering Xi Jinping's governance philosophy, mainland measures to combat telecommunications fraud, and other topics. They also visited several national-level museums and historical and cultural sites, to enhance participants' national confidence and sense of national identity.

In addition, under the arrangements of the Police College and the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government, in mid-May this year, 14 police officers and 23 personnel from various disciplined services also went to the China Executive Leadership Academy in Jinggangshan to participate in a disciplined services "Youth Backbone National Conditions Study Programme". The seven-day course covered topics including overall national development and national security, and participants also visited the Jiangxi Provincial Public Security Department.

Participants of the national conditions study programme visit the Nanchang August 1st Uprising Memorial Hall. (Police Bulletin photo)

When reporting its annual figures in February this year, the Immigration Department mentioned that in order to consolidate new-entry Immigration Officers' understanding of the national security concept, with the support of the Ministry of Public Security and the People's Police University of China, the department arranged for all trainees to participate in a national conditions and immigration management training course held at the People's Police University of China (Guangzhou); since mid-2025, the training arrangement has also covered all Immigration Assistant trainees, and the department arranged for a total of 257 personnel to undertake study and training at various mainland institutions throughout the year.

Information officers, civil aviation sector, education sector, Digital Commissioner also go to mainland for study programmes

In late June this year, 30 personnel from the Civil Aviation Department and the civil aviation industry management went to the National Academy of Governance in Beijing for a national conditions study programme, to deepen participants' understanding of the country's overall development and macro-strategic outlook. The seven-day course covered topics including national policy, security, diplomacy, technology and the latest developments in the civil aviation field, and also included on-site teaching at Beijing Daxing International Airport and three centres of the Civil Aviation Administration, with exchanges with officials and experts from mainland bodies.

In June this year, 30 personnel from the Civil Aviation Department and the civil aviation industry management went to the National Academy of Governance in Beijing for a national conditions study programme. (Photo courtesy of the Civil Aviation Department)

In addition, the Education Bureau and the "UNESCO Teacher Education Centre" established by the Shanghai municipal government have co-organised a study programme for STEAM education curriculum leaders, with eight sessions held to date, providing 275 training places. In June this year, over 30 principals, STEAM coordinators and teachers participated in the Shanghai study programme, learning about the development of innovation and technology education, the application of artificial intelligence in education, and other information.

In January this year, Director of Information Services Amy Liu also led information officers to Beijing to participate in a five-day "national conditions study programme", studying at Tsinghua University, visiting the State Council Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office where they were received by Director Xia Baolong, and then travelling to Chengdu for an investigation trip.

In early January this year, Director of Information Services Amy Liu led information officers to participate in a five-day "national conditions study programme", during which they were received by Director Xia Baolong. (Photo courtesy of the Information Services Department)

Digital Policy Commissioner Tony Wong also participated in the "2025 Hong Kong Information Technology and Cybersecurity Thematic Study Programme" at Zhejiang University in August 2025, with 30 industry representatives from government departments, public organisations and operators of various critical infrastructure enterprises participating. The seven-day itinerary included classroom teaching and on-site visits to innovation and technology enterprises in Hangzhou.
